title: Why Are We All So Stressed?

blanks.sentence: Overwhelm is described as an _____ linked to difficulty dealing with life.
A person may feel unable to handle their _____.
They might feel _____, as if too much is happening at once.
They may also feel they _____ with the pressure.
If the feeling lasts, it can become a form of _____.
Over time, this may finally lead to _____.
In exams, feeling stressed may not always be harmful; _____ can sharpen performance.
According to the advice, nerves may help students _____.
A realistic first step is accepting that a _____ will never completely disappear.
Having new tasks every day can simply be a sign of a _____.

multipleChoice.question: How is “overwhelm” defined in the extract?
options: A permanent illness caused by too much studying.
A state of struggling with the situation one is facing.
A short period of happiness after finishing tasks.
A habit of avoiding all difficult responsibilities.

multipleChoice.question: What risk is mentioned if overwhelm continues for a long time?
options: It may make people lose interest in all work immediately.
It may turn into a useful source of motivation.
It may stop people from feeling temporary pressure.
It may develop into chronic stress and eventually burnout.

multipleChoice.question: What surprising point is made about stress during an exam?
options: It may help some students perform better by focusing their mind.
It should be removed completely before students begin writing.
It usually makes students forget what they have learned.
It is useful only when the exam is not important.

multipleChoice.question: How do the speakers present “nerves” after the exam-stress advice?
options: As a sign that students have failed to prepare.
As a problem that only affects actors and athletes.
As worry that can sometimes support clearer thinking.
As a feeling that should be ignored during performance.

multipleChoice.question: What does the exchange suggest about advice for feeling overwhelmed?
options: There is one method that works best for everyone.
Different people may need different ways to handle it.
General stress can only be solved by finishing work faster.
The best solution is to stop making plans completely.

multipleChoice.question: What is Claudia’s first piece of general advice?
options: Complete every task before starting another one.
Keep the to-do list short by avoiding difficult tasks.
Treat tomorrow’s tasks as more important than today’s.
Accept that the to-do list will continue to exist.

multipleChoice.question: Why does Claudia say her advice “might sound defeatist”?
options: She realises accepting an endless list may sound negative.
She wants people to give up all their responsibilities.
She believes stress has no possible solution.
She is warning that busy people cannot be happy.

multipleChoice.question: What is implied by the idea that tomorrow will bring more tasks?
options: Most tasks are unnecessary and should be deleted.
People should finish tomorrow’s tasks today.
A continuing to-do list is a normal part of a busy life.
Stress mainly comes from poor time-management skills.

multipleChoice.question: Why does Neil suggest people should not stress too much about their to-do list?
options: Because written lists are less useful than memory.
Because new tasks will keep appearing anyway.
Because most tasks are easier than they look.
Because stress disappears when people work harder.

multipleChoice.question: Which broader message best matches the later advice on managing stress?
options: Stress can be avoided only by lowering all ambitions.
The best method is to use the same routine every day.
People should judge themselves by perfect productivity.
Managing stress can involve acceptance rather than total control.
